subject.title: [Feature]: Mobile apps: per-gateway custom headers for gateways behind authenticating proxies

question: Should native mobile gateway clients support arbitrary per-gateway custom headers, or should the first supported contract be a narrower typed proxy-auth surface such as Basic, Bearer, or fixed service-token headers?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but this changes a credential-bearing pre-Gateway-auth boundary and determines how secrets are stored, redacted, scoped, and attached on both mobile platforms.

options.title: Approve a typed proxy-auth contract first
options.body: Land platform work only after it narrows or documents the accepted credential shapes, TLS expectations, storage lifecycle, redaction, and gateway-only isolation.

options.title: Approve arbitrary per-gateway headers
options.body: Accept the broader operator-defined header surface after owner/security review signs off on reserved-header filtering, secret storage, diagnostics, and non-gateway isolation.

options.title: Defer native proxy credentials
options.body: Keep mobile reverse-proxy header injection unsupported for now and document VPN, Tailscale, or proxy-bypass alternatives while the security model remains unsettled.

recommendation.title: Approve a typed proxy-auth contract first
recommendation.body: Land platform work only after it narrows or documents the accepted credential shapes, TLS expectations, storage lifecycle, redaction, and gateway-only isolation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is assigned to the issue, authored the active platform PRs, and has the strongest current signal across this mobile gateway security/product boundary.
